description: This case study shows that separate simulation models of an ambulance service and hospital emergency departments can be run together as one distributed simulation, using London's emergency medical services as the case. Anastasia Anagnostou, Athar Nouman and Simon J. E. Taylor of Brunel University London presented it at the 2013 Winter Simulation Conference. An agent-based model of the ambulance service was coupled with several discrete-event models of accident and emergency departments, all built in the Repast Simphony toolkit, with the poRTIco run-time infrastructure handling communication between them. The aim was to allow integrated improvement scenarios across the emergency care chain and crisis management instead of studying each part in isolation. The conference paper is available online from IEEE by subscription or purchase; its abstract is free in OpenAlex. Coverage is the London emergency care system. Caveats: the models and data are not published, and the paper demonstrates feasibility, not a validated operational tool. The authors report that the distributed simulation successfully represented the real system. Simulation uses: an architecture for coupling ambulance and hospital models, relevant to co-simulation of emergency care under surge. Related records: the Newcastle multi-agency incident digital twin (case_study-newcastle-multi-agency-incident-digital-twin) and the Lazio ambulance location simulation (case_study-lazio-ares-118-ambulance-location-des) are other emergency service simulations.
